decisions.what: J-5 was excluded from a wave that had room for it, on a semantic-collision argument rather than a file-scope one.

decisions.what: Gate arms were built with `git archive` at the pre-dispatch commit instead of by copying the live tree.

Building both arms from a committed tree and overlaying only the one file under test makes the arms differ by exactly the change being judged. known_issues.desc: Subagents in this VPS -p session are sandboxed to the session --add-dir list (/opt/swarm, /opt/targets/aphorism-cli). A git worktree under /tmp is therefore UNREACHABLE to a builder: reads, bash, and EnterWorktree all refuse. Cycle 18 lost one builder dispatch to this. SKILL.md already prescribes "no worktrees" for headless sessions and gives disjoint file scopes as the concurrency answer instead; cycles 16-17 used /tmp worktrees anyway and cycle 18 is where it bit. Remedy for future cycles: at k_cap 1 let the single builder work directly in the target tree (conductor still sole committer); for k>1 headless, either scope builders to disjoint files in the one tree or place worktrees INSIDE an allowed directory.

Subagent scratch files land in the SWARM root (/opt/swarm) unless the dispatch prompt names an explicit scratch path. Hard rule 5 hands agents target paths only, but the session cwd IS /opt/swarm, so a relative scratch path silently lands inside the write fence -- the fence is enforced by what agents are TOLD, and cwd supplies what they were not told. Observed cycle 9 (builder used /opt/swarm/.scratch/) and again at cycles 17-18 (9 untracked .js/.json scratch files in the SWARM root, removed by the conductor at cycle 19). Harmless so far -- all occurrences were inert scratch, nothing under bin/, reference/, workflows/ or templates/ -- but the same reflex on a different task could write into SWARM tooling mid-run. CYCLE 36: control PASSES a third consecutive time. The dispatch prompt named an explicit scratch path (<target>/.swarm/scratch-c36/) and the builder used it; /opt/swarm stayed clean, verified by `git -C /opt/swarm status --porcelain`. The builder did NOT remove its own scratch tree this time (cycle 35's did), so the conductor removed it before commit -- the naming control is what is working; self-cleanup is not reliable and should not be assumed.
known_issues.note_cycle_21: THIRD occurrence, in a new and milder variant: the dispatch prompt named the explicit in-target scratch path as the remedy prescribes, and the builder honored it AND deleted its mutation copies -- but left the bare empty .swarm/scratch directory behind. Measured at 0 files inside, so nothing leaked and no untracked scratch reached git status; this is the same residue cycle 9 recorded (agent removes copies, conductor removes the empty directory). Caught only because the conductor gate carries a standing SCOPE.SCRATCH control, which is the reason to keep that control even on cycles where it looks like a formality. Remedy refinement for the wrap-up distillation: the prompt should say remove the scratch DIRECTORY, not just its contents.

known_issues.note_cycle_24: FOURTH occurrence, and it PARTIALLY CONTRADICTS the cycle-22 note below, so that note should not be read on its own. The cycle-21 remedy refinement was again applied verbatim in the dispatch prompt -- it named the in-target scratch path AND required removing the scratch DIRECTORY itself, not merely its contents, calling out that an empty directory counts as debris and is checked. The builder created three subdirectories under .swarm/scratch/ and reported removing them with rm -rf, which it had genuinely done: the standing SCOPE.SCRATCH control found .swarm/scratch present with ZERO entries inside. So the agent removed what it created and still left the parent it did not create. Nothing leaked, git status showed no untracked scratch, and the conductor removed the directory by hand. The lesson for the wrap-up distillation is narrower and more useful than 'name the scratch path': an agent told to remove its scratch directory removes the directories IT MADE, so the prompt must name the exact path whose absence is checked, or the check must tolerate an empty parent. Cycle 22's 'the remedy is now measured to work' was drawn from a single clean cycle and does not survive a second sample.

known_issues.desc: The conductor's sealed pre-dispatch baseline is READABLE BY THE BUILDER IT IS MEANT TO BE SEALED FROM. It is written to <target>/.swarm/runs/, which is inside the target directory every builder is given, so a builder that looks around the tree can read the exact cells the conductor committed to before dispatch. Observed cycle 31: the builder volunteered, unprompted, that it had noticed .swarm/backlog.json and two new .swarm/runs/ files and identified them as "the conductor/swarm tooling's own pre-dispatch baseline for this exact item", correctly naming cell B4 and its reading of 50. CYCLE 36 MITIGATION, which does NOT close the root cause: the conductor now uses commit-reveal -- seal written, sha256 committed before dispatch, plaintext DELETED for the whole dispatch window, rewritten and verified with `sha256sum -c` after the builder returns (OK at cycle 36). A deleted file cannot be read by any builder, so THIS cycle's seal was genuinely sealed. The root cause is untouched: <target>/.swarm/runs/ is still inside every builder's directory, every OTHER artefact there (prior gates, probes, baselines) is still readable, and the mitigation is conductor discipline rather than a structural boundary. A future conductor that forgets the delete step is back to KI-8 exactly as filed. The structural fix needs a scratch location outside the subagent sandbox that the conductor can also write, which this session does not have (KI-6 establishes /tmp is outside the sandbox; the Write tool is denied there).
known_issues.status: mitigated in practice, root cause open
known_issues.why_it_matters: Hard rule 2 rests on builders never having seen the check -- an agent that knows the check can code to it. The rule is enforced today by not PUTTING verify commands in the backlog, which is necessary but not sufficient: the baseline file is a second copy of much of the same information sitting in a directory the agent can read. This cycle it changed nothing and the honesty was exemplary -- the builder disclosed it rather than using it, and the decisive evidence (D1/D2) was authored AFTER dispatch and never written to disk until the gate ran, so the verdict is uncontaminated. But the integrity of the gate should not depend on a builder choosing to disclose.

known_issues.desc: CONDUCTOR-INSTRUMENT DEFECT, found at cycle 49 while rendering the dashboard. The LIVE per-target node in SWARM/runs/dashboard.html read "cycle 46 - 12 known issues open" while the run was at cycle 48. Cause: dashboard.html's first 112 lines are ONE HTML comment holding a legend with PLACEHOLDER copies of several live anchors, and runs/cycle47-dashboard.mjs matched the target node with /<div class="target"><b>\/opt\/targets\/aphorism-cli<\/b><span>[^<]*<\/span><\/div>/ -- no `g` flag and NO match-count assertion. String.replace with a non-global regex replaces only the FIRST match, and the first match in the file is the legend copy at line 38. So cycle 47 patched a comment nobody sees and left the human-visible node stale; cycle 48 reused the same script and repeated it. DISCRIMINATOR against "the render simply did not run": the legend copy WAS advanced to cycle 47 and then to cycle 48, so the writes landed -- they landed in the wrong region. This is precisely the KI-11 failure mode that runs/c46-dash.mjs's own header warns about in prose, three cycles before it happened; the warning existed and the assertion did not. REPAIRED IN THE ARTIFACT at cycle 49 (runs/c49-dash.mjs anchors the substitution on the `<!-- TARGETS -->` marker so it cannot reach the legend, and asserts an exact match count of 1 before replacing). WHAT REMAINS OPEN is the general defect: the dashboard is re-rendered by a hand-written per-cycle script, so the discipline is re-implemented from scratch every cycle and is only as good as the conductor's memory of it. A prose warning in one cycle's script does not carry to the next. Fix for a human: either strip the legend comment out of the published artifact, or give the anchors machine-distinguishable ids so a render cannot address the legend at all.

It is broader than that - the defect is that NOTHING asserts a render reached the live copy, so every region is exposed independently and each one fails silently on its own schedule. The durable repair is still a human's template edit (strip the legend from the published artifact, or give the live anchors machine-distinguishable ids); the cheap standing mitigation, which cost one script this cycle, is to RUN THE AUDIT AFTER EVERY RENDER and require every mandated region to report live=1.
